questions.prompt: During `tofu plan`, which statement about the proposed changes is accurate?

options.text: Plan is read-only: it shows what would change without applying.
options.rationale: Plan computes a diff against state and does not mutate remote infrastructure.
Only apply (or auto-approve flows) mutate infrastructure; plan does not.

options.text: Plan permanently locks state until apply completes.
options.rationale: State locking behaviour depends on backend configuration; plan itself is not a permanent lock.

questions.explanation: OpenTofu plan compares desired configuration to state and produces a change set; apply executes it.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish plan from apply in the core workflow.

questions.prompt: Why does OpenTofu store state separately from the configuration files?

options.text: State binds configuration to real-world resource identities and attributes.
options.rationale: Without state, OpenTofu cannot reliably map HCL to existing infrastructure.

options.text: State replaces HCL as the source of truth for desired configuration.
options.rationale: Configuration files express intent; state records what exists.

options.text: State exists primarily to encrypt provider credentials.
options.rationale: Credentials belong in environment or secret stores; state tracks resource metadata.

questions.explanation: State maps resource addresses to provider-specific IDs so subsequent plans can diff accurately.
questions.learningObjective: Explain why state is required beyond configuration alone.

questions.prompt: When should you extract repeated infrastructure into a module?

options.text: When the same composable pattern appears in multiple root modules.
options.rationale: Modules encapsulate reusable building blocks with a stable interface.

options.text: For every individual resource to keep root modules minimal.
options.rationale: Over-modularising single resources adds indirection without reuse benefit.

options.text: To prevent state from recording child module resources.
options.rationale: Child module resources still appear in state under the module address prefix.

questions.explanation: Modules reduce duplication and encode conventions; they do not bypass state tracking.
questions.learningObjective: Recognise when module extraction improves maintainability.
